# [Baseline] - WIN - D - Defender Additional Configuration

Defender settings that do not fit in the Endpoint Security template and therefore require a separate policy.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Windows |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | All Devices |
| checkId | `INTUNE-BASE-059-DDefenderAdditionalConfiguration` |
| Source | OpenIntuneBaseline Windows v4.0 — SC - Defender Antivirus - D - Additional Configuration |
| File | [`Baseline_WIN_D_Defender_Additional_Configuration.json`](Baseline_WIN_D_Defender_Additional_Configuration.json) |

> Settings that do not fit in the Endpoint Security antivirus template and therefore require a separate Settings Catalog policy. Since OIB v4.0: 'Disallow Exploit Protection Override' on (users could create exploit protection settings but could no longer remove them without admin rights), and 'Hide Exclusions From Local Users' removed because 'Hide Exclusions From Local Admins' already implies it.

## Standards

| Framework | Controls |
|---|---|
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.8.7 Protection against malware |
| NIS2 art. 21(2) | art. 21(2)(e) security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling |
| CIS Controls v8.1 | 10.1 Deploy and Maintain Anti-Malware Software<br>10.5 Enable Anti-Exploitation Features<br>10.6 Centrally Manage Anti-Malware Software |
| NIST CSF 2.0 | DE.CM-09 |

What this means per standard and what is needed organisationally alongside it: [COMPLIANCE.en.md](../../../COMPLIANCE.en.md).
